tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label and message are the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence; the detail goes in message. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

message.description: For a reply: what the click sends, up to 300 characters of plain text — no leading / or !. Omit when the label is the whole message.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

name.description: Tool name (e.g. computer, navigate, find, form_input, read_page). browser_batch cannot be nested. A tabs_create's new tabId is only returned when the batch ends — load that tab in a later call.

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

actions.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially. Example: [{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"left_click","ref":"ref_12"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"type","text":"hello"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"screenshot"}}]

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

    Data comes from public sources: IRS Form 990 filings and the IRS Business Master File,
    Canada's CRA charity filings and register, the Charity Commission for England and Wales,
    OSCR, the ACNC, Kenya's NGO board, 360Giving (UK), IATI, organizations' and funders' own
    websites, job boards, and government grant listings. Every tool only reads, except
    start_kindora_profile and start_connect_profile.

    TOOLS:
    - search_funders: grantmaking organizations by name, topic, or location
    - search_open_grants: open grant opportunities and RFPs by topic, cause area, or keywords
    - search_funder_jobs: open jobs at foundations (program officers, grants managers, CEOs)
    - search_nonprofits: the recipient side — nonprofits by cause, place, size, or funding
      received; `thesis` ranks them by a plain-language description
    - find_funders_of_nonprofit: who has funded one named nonprofit
    - search_organizations: nonprofits, NGOs and social enterprises in every country Kindora
      holds (US, Canada, UK, Australia, Kenya and more), by name, topic, country and role
    - get_organization_profile: one organization's full research profile: registrations,
      programs, quoted website facts, technology signals, and the funders that granted to it
    - find_funders_for_peers: funders that fund organizations like the user's
    - get_funder_profile, get_990_summary, get_foundation_grants, get_funder_stats:
      detail on one funder
    - get_ntee_codes: the NTEE cause-code list
    - start_kindora_profile: set up a nonprofit on Kindora from a brief, only when the person
      asks. It sends the person an email. Show them the whole brief and get their yes first.
    - start_connect_profile: set up a PERSON's Kindora Connect profile (one-to-one introductions)
      from a brief about them, only when the person asks. Same rule: show the brief, get their
      yes, then call. It sends the person an email; they confirm with a code, no password.

    CHOOSING THE RIGHT SEARCH TOOL:
    - Active grant opportunities or RFPs for a topic → search_open_grants
    - Funder organizations aligned to a topic, including funders with no live RFP →
      search_funders
    - A specific funder by name (e.g., "Ford Foundation") → search_funders
    - Who funds a specific nonprofit → find_funders_of_nonprofit
    - Peer nonprofits or a cause's landscape → search_nonprofits
    - A funder sourcing grantees, NGOs outside the US, or social enterprises →
      search_organizations, then get_organization_profile on the ones that fit
    - Jobs in philanthropy → search_funder_jobs
    - When exploring a cause area, run both search_funders and search_open_grants.

    BEST PRACTICES for search_open_grants:
    - Use `state` when the user has a known US location. For other countries use `country`
      as plain text (country="India"); state with a non-US country is rejected.
    - Describe what is wanted in natural language ("youth after school programs"). Quoted
      phrases match exactly; -term excludes ("education -higher").
    - Run several targeted searches rather than one broad one. Omit `query` to browse open
      programs by upcoming deadline.
    - Leave `source` unset unless asked: the foundation corpus is larger than government.

    BEST PRACTICES for search_funders:
    - `state` filters by the funder's US headquarters state.
    - `grantee_country_codes` (FIPS 10-4: "UK", "IN", "KE", "SF") finds funders whose grantees
      are in a non-US country ("who funds work in India?").

input.message:
Read `[[Spec: MCP token handoff]]` (uid `kPg_0_-lh`, 9 linked refs) in full via get_page. Report below covers only that page.

## 1. Structure / format

It is **OpenSpec-format, but with the sections ordered Proposal → Specs → Design → Tasks** (the spec block sits between Proposal and Design, not after Design). Four H2s:

- **Proposal** (`NZMOpbT2i`) → H3s: Why, What Changes, Settled and open decisions, Capabilities, Impact
- **Spec: mcp-session-access** (`GYtOqf4U2`) → H3s: Purpose, ADDED Requirements (5 requirements, each with WHEN/THEN/AND scenarios and a `Source:` line)
- **Design** (`-0hMsmA6D`) → H3s: Context, Goals / Non-Goals, Decisions (5), Risks / Trade-offs (6), Migration Plan
- **Tasks** (`Dw-EclQK6`) → groups 0–5, Roam `{{[[DONE]]}}` / `{{[[TODO]]}}` checkboxes

Capability name introduced: **`mcp-session-access`** (new); Modified Capabilities: "None."

Every requirement, decision and task is annotated **"Source: no ticket yet."** / "(No ticket.)" — the page states "No Linear ticket exists yet… Tickets are created from this change."

## 2. The handoff flow (exact)

1. User runs a **"Connect MCP" command** in a plugin that is signed in as the space account, and **chooses a label** (example used throughout: `"Laptop MCP"`).
2. A shared helper (to live next to `createLoggedInClient` in `packages/database/src/lib/contextFunctions.ts`) creates a **second Supabase client with `persistSession: false` and `autoRefreshToken: false`**, signs in with `signInWithPassword` using the space account email (`spaceAnonUserEmail`) + space password — i.e. a genuinely new `auth.sessions` row, not a copy of the plugin's.
   - Rationale given verbatim: "A persisting client would overwrite the plugin's stored session. An auto-refreshing one would rotate the refresh token after it was handed over and break the MCP."
3. That new session calls **`register_mcp_session(label TEXT)`** (SECURITY DEFINER, granted to `authenticated`), which reads **`session_id` and `sub` from `auth.jwt()`** and inserts the registry row. So a caller can only ever register *itself* — "cannot plant a plugin's session ID in the registry so that it can later be signed out as an MCP."
4. The helper then **discards the client without signing out**, and returns the **handoff bundle**: **Supabase URL, anon key, space ID, and the new session's refresh token** (exactly these four).
5. The plugin **shows the bundle once**, with a copy button, and **stores no copy of the refresh token**. The plugin's own session is unchanged and not replaced in storage.
6. The MCP ends up holding **only that bundle** — i.e. a refresh token for a dedicated space-account session. It refreshes to get access tokens. The bundle's original refresh token stops working "once the rotation grace period has passed" (rotation is on, `refresh_token_reuse_interval = 10`), so the MCP must persist every rotated refresh token or it loses the session after its first refresh.

Where things are stored today (Context section, read from code 2026-10-31): Roam keeps the space password in **block props on the settings page** (`getOrCreateSpacePassword` in `apps/roam/src/utils/supabaseContext.ts`); Obsidian in **`plugin.settings.spacePassword`**. The MCP never receives the password — that is an explicit Goal.

## 3. The `mcp_session` table (exact columns)

```
session_id UUID PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES auth.sessions(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
account_id UUID NOT NULL          -- the space account
label      TEXT NOT NULL
created    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
```
- RLS: `SELECT` allowed where `account_id = auth.uid()`. **No client gets direct `INSERT`, `UPDATE` or `DELETE`.**
- The `ON DELETE CASCADE` removes the row when Supabase deletes the session, including on the MCP's own local-scope sign-out.
- Purpose, stated explicitly: a session's ID "appears only in its own tokens, and `auth.sessions` does not record which sessions were handed to an MCP. A session that was not registered at handoff therefore cannot be identified later." So **the table + registration ship in v0 even if per-session sign-out is postponed** (settled by Marc-Antoine Parent, 2026-10-31), so that sign-out added later can still cover every session already handed over.

## 4. What the MCP can do — and what constrains it

**Full permissions of the space account — read AND write.** Stated three times:
- Proposal: "This is v0. The MCP gets the full permissions of the space account."
- Settled decision: "v0 grants the full permissions of the space account."
- Non-Goal: "Restricting what the MCP can do. v0 gives the full permissions of the space account. Restriction belongs to `agent-read-only-access`."

The opening Why states the aim is "an MCP server to **read and write** a space's discourse graph in Supabase on behalf of that space."

Constraints in v0 are only these:
- It is a session, not the password, so it can be signed out without rotating the space password.
- *Proposed, not settled*: it must not be able to change the space password (see below).
- In v0 as proposed there is **no per-MCP revocation at all** — only the emergency `signOut({ scope: 'others' })`, which also signs out every plugin instance of the space (they then sign back in with the space password).

## 5. Revocation / sign-out and timing

Three mechanisms:
- **Per-session sign-out** (*proposed for immediately after v0, timing unsettled*): `sign_out_mcp_session(session_id UUID) RETURNS BOOLEAN`, `SECURITY DEFINER`, granted to `authenticated` only. Deletes from `auth.sessions` where `id = session_id` **AND** `user_id = auth.uid()` **AND** a matching `mcp_session` row exists; returns whether a row was deleted. An unregistered session ID → nothing is ended and the call reports nothing signed out.
- **Self sign-out** (in v0 scope, requirement "An MCP can sign itself out"): standard Supabase sign-out with **local scope**; its registry row then disappears via the cascade.
- **Emergency switch**: `signOut({ scope: 'others' })` — signs out every other session of the space account, including all plugin instances.

**Speed:** revocation takes effect at the MCP's **next refresh**, which fails. Already-issued access tokens stay valid until they expire — **up to `jwt_expiry` = 3600 s (one hour)**. Listed as an accepted risk: "`jwt_expiry` could be shortened for all users if needed." Ending already-issued access tokens is an explicit Non-Goal.

Rejected revocation options on record: (b) custom access token hook with a `revoked_at` column refusing tokens for revoked sessions — deferred, "kept for when restricted accounts need a token claim: the `mcp_session` table is the place it would read"; (c) `signOut({ scope: 'others' })` only.

**Password-change escape hatch** (a substantial sub-decision, "Can the MCP change the space password?"): with `secure_password_change = false` (today's setting), any space-account session can `PUT /auth/v1/user` and set a new password, then sign in with it and get sessions not in the registry — defeating per-session sign-out — while also signing out every other session (`LogoutAllExceptMe` in `internal/models/user.go`) and locking the plugins out.
- Part 1 (settled, MAP 2026-10-31): turn on `secure_password_change`. Verified against `supabase/auth` at `a7e97d6` (2026-10-30), `UserUpdate` in `internal/api/user.go`: a nonce is required only when `session.CreatedAt` is >24h old, and a refresh does not create a new session so the clock starts at handoff and never resets; the nonce goes to the account email, which space accounts cannot receive. **So for the first 24 hours after handoff the MCP can still change the password.**
- Part 2 (settled, MAP 2026-10-31): also turn on **"require current password"** (`security_update_password_require_current_password` in the Management API; `UpdatePasswordRequireCurrentPassword` in source) — refuses a password change without the current password except in a recovery session. Shipped in `supabase/auth` **PR 2364 (2026-02-11), in v2.197.0**. This closes the first-24-hours gap.
- **Catch:** the Supabase CLI's `config.toml` has **no key** for this setting (checked in `supabase/cli` main, `packages/config/src/auth/email.ts`) — hosted-project/dashboard/Management-API only, so it **cannot be proven by a local cucumber scenario**.

## 6. Transport and clients

The page **does not discuss stdio vs remote HTTP at all**, and names no MCP client product (no Claude Desktop/Cursor/etc.). It is transport-agnostic by construction: "Building the MCP server itself" is an explicit **Non-Goal** — "This change only defines the bundle it receives."

What the shape implies and the page does say: the bundle is pasted by the user into the MCP, the MCP is a Supabase client that refreshes directly against the project, and **it must run as a single instance per bundle** (otherwise two copies refreshing with the same token outside the 10 s reuse interval trip Supabase's reuse detection and may revoke the session). Task 4.1 is to document "the bundle format and the client settings the MCP must use." The "clients" named are the *plugins* that do the handing over: `apps/roam` and `apps/obsidian` (tasks 3.1/3.2, 5.2/5.3).

## 7. Effort estimates, tasks, blockers, open questions, risks

**Effort estimates — only one appears on the whole page**, on task group 5: "About **1.25 days** in one app, plus about the same as 5.2 for a second app." Groups 0–4 (the actual v0 work) carry **no day estimates**.

**Task list** (groups are the proposed ticket boundaries):
- **0. Decisions before tickets** — 0.1 DONE (`secure_password_change` on), 0.2 DONE (require current password on, so 5.5 stays), 0.3 DONE (every user may connect), **0.4 TODO** — settle whether per-session sign-out and the password settings stay out of v0; "This needs a group decision."
- **1. Database: registry** — 1.1 table + FK + RLS + `COMMENT ON` + migration (verify `supabase db reset`, select isolation); 1.2 `register_mcp_session(label)` (cucumber: registration + cross-space isolation); 1.3 regenerate `dbTypes`, `check-types` passes.
- **2. Shared handoff helper** — 2.1 helper next to `createLoggedInClient` (vitest/cucumber: caller's stored session unchanged, bundle token refreshes once).
- **3. Plugin UI** — 3.1 Roam "Connect MCP" command, label prompt, bundle shown once with copy button, offered to every user (verify: live demo in a test graph with a script refreshing from the bundle); 3.2 Obsidian same, test vault.
- **4. MCP side** — 4.1 document bundle format + required client settings (persist every rotated refresh token, single instance, local-scope sign-out on disconnect); verify with a minimal script that refreshes, signs out, and then has no registry row.
- **5. Proposed for immediately after v0** — 5.1 `sign_out_mcp_session`, plus "confirm on a hosted branch project that `postgres` can delete from `auth.sessions`"; 5.2 Roam settings list with per-session sign-out button; 5.3 Obsidian same; 5.4 `secure_password_change = true` locally + hosted (verify by editing `auth.sessions.created_at` to age a session past 24 h, expect "Password update requires reauthentication"); 5.5 turn on require-current-password on the hosted project, record that the local stack cannot set it, "Test with a throwaway space, not a real one."

**Ticket IDs named (only two, neither a hard blocker):**
- **ENG-2437** — task 1.2: "Don't revoke from `anon` until ENG-2437 lands: check `auth.uid()` inside the function instead." This is the one sequencing dependency on the page.
- **ENG-1834** — cited only as the source of a client-side admin check, in the rejected option (b) for "Who in a space may connect an MCP."

**Open question (exactly one):** block `JB4OOyCIl` / task 0.4 — whether per-session sign-out and the two password settings stay out of v0. Proposal dated **2026-11-02**: do both immediately after v0, "because full access without revocation is held to be an acceptable v0 baseline." The table and registration ship in v0 either way.

**Risks / Trade-offs (6, verbatim headings):**
1. No way to cut off one MCP in v0 → proposed as acceptable; emergency switch remains.
2. Without the password settings, a v0 MCP can change the space password → locks out every plugin instance and the MCP can sign back in with the new password; proposed as acceptable for the short time before the next step.
3. After the next step, a signed-out MCP keeps access for up to an hour → accepted; `jwt_expiry` could be shortened for all users.
4. Foreign key from `public` to `auth.sessions` → Supabase owns that schema and may change it; fallback is to drop the FK and have the listing join `auth.sessions` inside a `SECURITY DEFINER` function to hide rows whose session is gone.
5. The bundle is a bearer secret → shown once, not stored; the MCP must store it safely and save every rotated refresh token.
6. Refresh token reuse window → two copies refreshing outside the 10 s interval may get the session revoked; run a single instance per bundle.

**Migration plan:** additive — one table, one function, one migration (second function in the next step). Rollback drops them. Sessions already handed over keep working until signed out, "because nothing in Supabase Auth depends on the table."

**Impact surfaces:** `packages/database/supabase/schemas/` (table, RLS, registration fn, migration, `dbTypes` regen); `packages/database/src/lib/` (helper beside `createLoggedInClient` in `contextFunctions.ts`); `apps/roam` + `apps/obsidian` (connect command, later the sessions list); Supabase project config (`config.toml` + hosted). **Not affected: the website and Edge Functions.**

## 8. How it positions itself against the other two specs

- **vs. agent read-only access** (`[[[[ISS]] - Spec: Agent read-only access]]`): "The read-only, revocable agent accounts planned in [that spec] stay the long-term answer. **This change does not depend on them and does not block them.**" Restriction of MCP powers is handed off wholesale: Non-Goal "Restriction belongs to `agent-read-only-access`." It also borrows two findings from that spec rather than redoing them: that the project uses **asymmetric keys whose private half cannot be extracted** (which is why option (a), a self-signed long-lived JWT, was rejected — unrevokable short of rotating the signing key), and that `agent-read-only-access` "records the same endpoint behaviour in its design" for `PUT /auth/v1/user`. The deferred custom-access-token-hook option is explicitly held "for when restricted accounts need a token claim."
- **vs. the headless retrieval API / MCP design page (`LPDwCRT6_`)**: **no reference to it anywhere on this page** — not by title, not by link. Read `[[Spec: MCP token handoff]]` (uid `kPg_0_-lh`, 9 linked refs) in full via get_page. Report below covers only that page.

## 1. Structure / format

It is **OpenSpec-format, but with the sections ordered Proposal → Specs → Design → Tasks** (the spec block sits between Proposal and Design, not after Design). Four H2s:

- **Proposal** (`NZMOpbT2i`) → H3s: Why, What Changes, Settled and open decisions, Capabilities, Impact
- **Spec: mcp-session-access** (`GYtOqf4U2`) → H3s: Purpose, ADDED Requirements (5 requirements, each with WHEN/THEN/AND scenarios and a `Source:` line)
- **Design** (`-0hMsmA6D`) → H3s: Context, Goals / Non-Goals, Decisions (5), Risks / Trade-offs (6), Migration Plan
- **Tasks** (`Dw-EclQK6`) → groups 0–5, Roam `{{[[DONE]]}}` / `{{[[TODO]]}}` checkboxes

Capability name introduced: **`mcp-session-access`** (new); Modified Capabilities: "None."

Every requirement, decision and task is annotated **"Source: no ticket yet."** / "(No ticket.)" — the page states "No Linear ticket exists yet… Tickets are created from this change."

## 2. The handoff flow (exact)

1. User runs a **"Connect MCP" command** in a plugin that is signed in as the space account, and **chooses a label** (example used throughout: `"Laptop MCP"`).
2. A shared helper (to live next to `createLoggedInClient` in `packages/database/src/lib/contextFunctions.ts`) creates a **second Supabase client with `persistSession: false` and `autoRefreshToken: false`**, signs in with `signInWithPassword` using the space account email (`spaceAnonUserEmail`) + space password — i.e. a genuinely new `auth.sessions` row, not a copy of the plugin's.
   - Rationale given verbatim: "A persisting client would overwrite the plugin's stored session. An auto-refreshing one would rotate the refresh token after it was handed over and break the MCP."
3. That new session calls **`register_mcp_session(label TEXT)`** (SECURITY DEFINER, granted to `authenticated`), which reads **`session_id` and `sub` from `auth.jwt()`** and inserts the registry row. So a caller can only ever register *itself* — "cannot plant a plugin's session ID in the registry so that it can later be signed out as an MCP."
4. The helper then **discards the client without signing out**, and returns the **handoff bundle**: **Supabase URL, anon key, space ID, and the new session's refresh token** (exactly these four).
5. The plugin **shows the bundle once**, with a copy button, and **stores no copy of the refresh token**. The plugin's own session is unchanged and not replaced in storage.
6. The MCP ends up holding **only that bundle** — i.e. a refresh token for a dedicated space-account session. It refreshes to get access tokens. The bundle's original refresh token stops working "once the rotation grace period has passed" (rotation is on, `refresh_token_reuse_interval = 10`), so the MCP must persist every rotated refresh token or it loses the session after its first refresh.

Where things are stored today (Context section, read from code 2026-10-31): Roam keeps the space password in **block props on the settings page** (`getOrCreateSpacePassword` in `apps/roam/src/utils/supabaseContext.ts`); Obsidian in **`plugin.settings.spacePassword`**. The MCP never receives the password — that is an explicit Goal.

## 3. The `mcp_session` table (exact columns)

```
session_id UUID PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES auth.sessions(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
account_id UUID NOT NULL          -- the space account
label      TEXT NOT NULL
created    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
```
- RLS: `SELECT` allowed where `account_id = auth.uid()`. **No client gets direct `INSERT`, `UPDATE` or `DELETE`.**
- The `ON DELETE CASCADE` removes the row when Supabase deletes the session, including on the MCP's own local-scope sign-out.
- Purpose, stated explicitly: a session's ID "appears only in its own tokens, and `auth.sessions` does not record which sessions were handed to an MCP. A session that was not registered at handoff therefore cannot be identified later." So **the table + registration ship in v0 even if per-session sign-out is postponed** (settled by Marc-Antoine Parent, 2026-10-31), so that sign-out added later can still cover every session already handed over.

## 4. What the MCP can do — and what constrains it

**Full permissions of the space account — read AND write.** Stated three times:
- Proposal: "This is v0. The MCP gets the full permissions of the space account."
- Settled decision: "v0 grants the full permissions of the space account."
- Non-Goal: "Restricting what the MCP can do. v0 gives the full permissions of the space account. Restriction belongs to `agent-read-only-access`."

The opening Why states the aim is "an MCP server to **read and write** a space's discourse graph in Supabase on behalf of that space."

Constraints in v0 are only these:
- It is a session, not the password, so it can be signed out without rotating the space password.
- *Proposed, not settled*: it must not be able to change the space password (see below).
- In v0 as proposed there is **no per-MCP revocation at all** — only the emergency `signOut({ scope: 'others' })`, which also signs out every plugin instance of the space (they then sign back in with the space password).

## 5. Revocation / sign-out and timing

Three mechanisms:
- **Per-session sign-out** (*proposed for immediately after v0, timing unsettled*): `sign_out_mcp_session(session_id UUID) RETURNS BOOLEAN`, `SECURITY DEFINER`, granted to `authenticated` only. Deletes from `auth.sessions` where `id = session_id` **AND** `user_id = auth.uid()` **AND** a matching `mcp_session` row exists; returns whether a row was deleted. An unregistered session ID → nothing is ended and the call reports nothing signed out.
- **Self sign-out** (in v0 scope, requirement "An MCP can sign itself out"): standard Supabase sign-out with **local scope**; its registry row then disappears via the cascade.
- **Emergency switch**: `signOut({ scope: 'others' })` — signs out every other session of the space account, including all plugin instances.

**Speed:** revocation takes effect at the MCP's **next refresh**, which fails. Already-issued access tokens stay valid until they expire — **up to `jwt_expiry` = 3600 s (one hour)**. Listed as an accepted risk: "`jwt_expiry` could be shortened for all users if needed." Ending already-issued access tokens is an explicit Non-Goal.

Rejected revocation options on record: (b) custom access token hook with a `revoked_at` column refusing tokens for revoked sessions — deferred, "kept for when restricted accounts need a token claim: the `mcp_session` table is the place it would read"; (c) `signOut({ scope: 'others' })` only.

**Password-change escape hatch** (a substantial sub-decision, "Can the MCP change the space password?"): with `secure_password_change = false` (today's setting), any space-account session can `PUT /auth/v1/user` and set a new password, then sign in with it and get sessions not in the registry — defeating per-session sign-out — while also signing out every other session (`LogoutAllExceptMe` in `internal/models/user.go`) and locking the plugins out.
- Part 1 (settled, MAP 2026-10-31): turn on `secure_password_change`. Verified against `supabase/auth` at `a7e97d6` (2026-10-30), `UserUpdate` in `internal/api/user.go`: a nonce is required only when `session.CreatedAt` is >24h old, and a refresh does not create a new session so the clock starts at handoff and never resets; the nonce goes to the account email, which space accounts cannot receive. **So for the first 24 hours after handoff the MCP can still change the password.**
- Part 2 (settled, MAP 2026-10-31): also turn on **"require current password"** (`security_update_password_require_current_password` in the Management API; `UpdatePasswordRequireCurrentPassword` in source) — refuses a password change without the current password except in a recovery session. Shipped in `supabase/auth` **PR 2364 (2026-02-11), in v2.197.0**. This closes the first-24-hours gap.
- **Catch:** the Supabase CLI's `config.toml` has **no key** for this setting (checked in `supabase/cli` main, `packages/config/src/auth/email.ts`) — hosted-project/dashboard/Management-API only, so it **cannot be proven by a local cucumber scenario**.

## 6. Transport and clients

The page **does not discuss stdio vs remote HTTP at all**, and names no MCP client product (no Claude Desktop/Cursor/etc.). It is transport-agnostic by construction: "Building the MCP server itself" is an explicit **Non-Goal** — "This change only defines the bundle it receives."

What the shape implies and the page does say: the bundle is pasted by the user into the MCP, the MCP is a Supabase client that refreshes directly against the project, and **it must run as a single instance per bundle** (otherwise two copies refreshing with the same token outside the 10 s reuse interval trip Supabase's reuse detection and may revoke the session). Task 4.1 is to document "the bundle format and the client settings the MCP must use." The "clients" named are the *plugins* that do the handing over: `apps/roam` and `apps/obsidian` (tasks 3.1/3.2, 5.2/5.3).

## 7. Effort estimates, tasks, blockers, open questions, risks

**Effort estimates — only one appears on the whole page**, on task group 5: "About **1.25 days** in one app, plus about the same as 5.2 for a second app." Groups 0–4 (the actual v0 work) carry **no day estimates**.

**Task list** (groups are the proposed ticket boundaries):
- **0. Decisions before tickets** — 0.1 DONE (`secure_password_change` on), 0.2 DONE (require current password on, so 5.5 stays), 0.3 DONE (every user may connect), **0.4 TODO** — settle whether per-session sign-out and the password settings stay out of v0; "This needs a group decision."
- **1. Database: registry** — 1.1 table + FK + RLS + `COMMENT ON` + migration (verify `supabase db reset`, select isolation); 1.2 `register_mcp_session(label)` (cucumber: registration + cross-space isolation); 1.3 regenerate `dbTypes`, `check-types` passes.
- **2. Shared handoff helper** — 2.1 helper next to `createLoggedInClient` (vitest/cucumber: caller's stored session unchanged, bundle token refreshes once).
- **3. Plugin UI** — 3.1 Roam "Connect MCP" command, label prompt, bundle shown once with copy button, offered to every user (verify: live demo in a test graph with a script refreshing from the bundle); 3.2 Obsidian same, test vault.
- **4. MCP side** — 4.1 document bundle format + required client settings (persist every rotated refresh token, single instance, local-scope sign-out on disconnect); verify with a minimal script that refreshes, signs out, and then has no registry row.
- **5. Proposed for immediately after v0** — 5.1 `sign_out_mcp_session`, plus "confirm on a hosted branch project that `postgres` can delete from `auth.sessions`"; 5.2 Roam settings list with per-session sign-out button; 5.3 Obsidian same; 5.4 `secure_password_change = true` locally + hosted (verify by editing `auth.sessions.created_at` to age a session past 24 h, expect "Password update requires reauthentication"); 5.5 turn on require-current-password on the hosted project, record that the local stack cannot set it, "Test with a throwaway space, not a real one."

**Ticket IDs named (only two, neither a hard blocker):**
- **ENG-2437** — task 1.2: "Don't revoke from `anon` until ENG-2437 lands: check `auth.uid()` inside the function instead." This is the one sequencing dependency on the page.
- **ENG-1834** — cited only as the source of a client-side admin check, in the rejected option (b) for "Who in a space may connect an MCP."

**Open question (exactly one):** block `JB4OOyCIl` / task 0.4 — whether per-session sign-out and the two password settings stay out of v0. Proposal dated **2026-11-02**: do both immediately after v0, "because full access without revocation is held to be an acceptable v0 baseline." The table and registration ship in v0 either way.

**Risks / Trade-offs (6, verbatim headings):**
1. No way to cut off one MCP in v0 → proposed as acceptable; emergency switch remains.
2. Without the password settings, a v0 MCP can change the space password → locks out every plugin instance and the MCP can sign back in with the new password; proposed as acceptable for the short time before the next step.
3. After the next step, a signed-out MCP keeps access for up to an hour → accepted; `jwt_expiry` could be shortened for all users.
4. Foreign key from `public` to `auth.sessions` → Supabase owns that schema and may change it; fallback is to drop the FK and have the listing join `auth.sessions` inside a `SECURITY DEFINER` function to hide rows whose session is gone.
5. The bundle is a bearer secret → shown once, not stored; the MCP must store it safely and save every rotated refresh token.
6. Refresh token reuse window → two copies refreshing outside the 10 s interval may get the session revoked; run a single instance per bundle.

**Migration plan:** additive — one table, one function, one migration (second function in the next step). Rollback drops them. Sessions already handed over keep working until signed out, "because nothing in Supabase Auth depends on the table."

**Impact surfaces:** `packages/database/supabase/schemas/` (table, RLS, registration fn, migration, `dbTypes` regen); `packages/database/src/lib/` (helper beside `createLoggedInClient` in `contextFunctions.ts`); `apps/roam` + `apps/obsidian` (connect command, later the sessions list); Supabase project config (`config.toml` + hosted). **Not affected: the website and Edge Functions.**

## 8. How it positions itself against the other two specs

- **vs. agent read-only access** (`[[[[ISS]] - Spec: Agent read-only access]]`): "The read-only, revocable agent accounts planned in [that spec] stay the long-term answer. **This change does not depend on them and does not block them.**" Restriction of MCP powers is handed off wholesale: Non-Goal "Restriction belongs to `agent-read-only-access`." It also borrows two findings from that spec rather than redoing them: that the project uses **asymmetric keys whose private half cannot be extracted** (which is why option (a), a self-signed long-lived JWT, was rejected — unrevokable short of rotating the signing key), and that `agent-read-only-access` "records the same endpoint behaviour in its design" for `PUT /auth/v1/user`. The deferred custom-access-token-hook option is explicitly held "for when restricted accounts need a token claim."
- **vs. the headless retrieval API / MCP design page (`LPDwCRT6_`)**: **no reference to it anywhere on this page** — not by title, not by link. The only gesture in that direction is the Non-Goal "Building the MCP server itself. This change only defines the bundle it receives." So this spec is strictly the auth/credential layer beneath whatever MCP server that design describes, and does not claim a relationship to it.

It would only hide the command."
